_comment: USER-FOUND, 2026-09-03 (play viewer, EldraziDisplacerFlicker seed 1 turn 3): a hand-played
combo turn the engine could not reach, because a cast's GENERIC pip ate the board's only
flexible mana and banked a colourless one instead.
THE CAUSE: SpendFloatingTowardCost drains generic pips WILD FIRST. That order is right where it
was written for -- the whole-turn batch pre-payment, where `wild` IS the batch's own generic
requirement and draining it first stops an early cast's generic pip from eating a later cast's
pinned colour. It is exactly backwards at the OTHER caller, TapForCostBacktrackWorker's
out_leftover: that one is not paying anything. The tap set is chosen and the cost is already
known payable; it only decides which produced mana counts as spent, and therefore what the rest
of the main phase inherits. Wild-first there spends the unit that could pay any colour and banks
the one that can pay almost nothing. MTG_KEEP_FLEXIBLE_FLOAT (default on) inverts it for that
call only.
ON THE REAL BOARD: Aether Hub carrying a Wild Growth and a Trace of Abundance taps for {C}{G}
plus one wild. Living Wish {1}{G} took the {G} for its coloured pip and then took the WILD for
its generic, leaving {C}. With Mariposa's {C} that is two colourless against Cloud of Faeries'
{1}{U} -- unpayable, and the combo turn stopped there. Spending the {C} instead leaves the wild,
which pays the {U} while Mariposa pays the {1}. Verified on the live game: turn 3 now offers
'cast: Cloud of Faeries' where it previously offered only 'cycle Cloud of Faeries to draw'.
WHY THIS FIXTURE IS SHAPED LIKE THIS. The obvious fixture -- one plan casting both spells --
does NOT discriminate: the batch pre-payment solves the turn's costs JOINTLY and finds the good
assignment either way. The bug needs two SEPARATE payments, which is what the real board had
(Living Wish FETCHES Cloud of Faeries, so it is not a known cast and the joint solve cannot
cover it by construction). A cast plus a battlefield ACTIVATION reproduces that split without
needing a tutor: activations are paid in the trailing pass, out of whatever the casts left.
Neither does `validate_line`: CheckLine grades affordability with its own greedy sim, not the
real payment path, so it verdicts `accept` on both arms. The assertion has to be BEHAVIOURAL,
which is why this pins opponent_life.
THE BOARD is built so every choice is forced. Aether Hub's Wild Growth is the only GREEN, so
Muscle Sliver {1}{G} must tap the Hub; Trace of Abundance's wild is the only RED, so Shivan
Gorge's '{2}{R}, {T}: deals 1 damage to each opponent' can only be paid from what that cast left
behind. Mana is exact: Hub 3 + two Mariposa 2 = 5 against {1}{G} + {2}{R} = 5. (Shivan Gorge's
own {C} is NOT in that total -- it taps for its own ability; see PermAbilityTapDebitOf and
tap_ability_self_funding_unpayable.json.) max_turns is set to the staged turn so the 1/1 never
attacks and opponent_life moves only via the Gorge.
Verified DISCRIMINATING: MTG_KEEP_FLEXIBLE_FLOAT=1 -> opponent_life 19 (the Gorge fires),
MTG_KEEP_FLEXIBLE_FLOAT=0 -> opponent_life 20 (no red on the board, activation unpayable).
Shivan Gorge is not an arbitrary choice of payoff: it is EldraziDisplacerFlicker's lethal outlet,
so the mana this bug threw away is damage.
